# The Producer's Journey: From Messy Files to a Running Pipeline

This page explains the *logic* of how the four user spaces — TEST_LAB, GALLERY, BLUEPRINT,
and HOME — fit together for the person who **produces** an analysis pipeline, as opposed to
the HOME scientist who **runs** a finished one. Full design detail (open questions,
alternatives considered): `.claude/design/developer_workflow.md`.

## 1. A map, not a wizard

Every tool below is independently useful and can be entered directly. If you only need to
convert an Excel file to TSV, use the Reformatter and stop there. If you only need synthetic
test data, use AquaSynthesizer and stop there. Nothing forces you through stages you do not
need — each tool runs to completion and hands you a downloadable file; closing its panel
resets it to empty, with no hidden state carried forward.

## 2. The four stages

```
   STAGE 1              STAGE 2            STAGE 3               STAGE 4
   Prepare data         Scaffold           Build pipeline        Run
   (TEST_LAB)           (TEST_LAB)         (BLUEPRINT)           (HOME)
   ───────────          ──────────         ──────────────        ──────────
   Reformat             Data analysis      Add wrangling/joins   Load data analysis recipe
   Reconcile IDs  ───►   recipe      ───►  Add plots/groups ───► Run analysis
   Anonymise            Scaffolding        Preview / validate    Filter + audit
   Synthesise           (boilerplate)      Save data analysis    Export (with provenance)
                                            recipe
                                                ▲
                                                │ inspiration (copy YAML)
                                           ┌────┴─────┐
                                           │ GALLERY  │
                                           └──────────┘
```

| Stage | What it does | Standalone use |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Prepare data** (TEST_LAB) | Reformatter cleans XLSX/CSV to TSV; ID Reconciliation checks IDs line up across files and produces a reusable id transformation; Anonymiser strips identifying columns; AquaSynthesizer generates demo or stress-test data. | "I just need clean TSVs" / "Do my files' IDs match?" / "Make this safe to share" / "Give me test data." |
| **2. Scaffold** (TEST_LAB) | Data analysis recipe Scaffolding turns prepared files (plus an optional id transformation) into a *boilerplate* data analysis recipe ZIP — structure, inferred column types, primary-key hints, and ID-cleaning steps. It never generates analysis groups, plots, or the join strategy — that is your job in BLUEPRINT. | "Give me a starting point, not a finished pipeline." |
| **3. Build pipeline** (BLUEPRINT) | Open the boilerplate and build the real pipeline with no code: add wrangling/join/plot nodes through forms, organise groups, preview on Apply, validate, save. GALLERY feeds this stage as *inspiration* — browse a worked example, copy its YAML, adapt it. | "I have files and a scientific goal; build me a pipeline." |
| **4. Run** (HOME) | Load the finished data analysis recipe, explore and filter, send decisions to the audit trail with a reason, export with full provenance. | The consumer end — this is what the HOME scientist does with what you built. |

## 3. Recommended orderings — advice, never a gate

Some tools have a logical prerequisite: using them in that order gives correct results, but
nothing stops you from skipping it if your data does not need it.

| If you want to… | Do this first | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Anonymise several related files | Reconcile IDs | Anonymisation must map the same original ID to the same anonymised ID in every file, or joins break after anonymising. Reconciliation confirms the IDs actually line up before you replace them. |
| Scaffold a data analysis recipe with joins | Reconcile IDs | The scaffolder bakes a verified join key and ID-cleaning steps into `tier1`; without reconciliation it has nothing to bake. |
| Reconcile messy-format files | Reformat | Reconciliation needs clean tabular TSVs, not an XLSX or an odd-delimiter CSV. |
| Test a pipeline you are building | Synthesise data | Stress-test data exercises error handling before real data is loaded. |

A developer with already-clean, already-aligned data skips Reconciliation entirely — it is
frequently the first step, never a mandatory one.

## 4. How the stages actually link: export, then choose

There is **no in-app "Send to" button** moving a result straight from one tool into the next,
and no automatic injection. Linking is deliberately simple:

1. A tool runs and **exports** its result — a TSV, a step-list YAML, a data analysis recipe ZIP.
2. You **choose** that file as the input to the next tool, exactly as you would choose any
   file from disk.

This keeps every tool a genuinely independent module: each picks its own input and produces
its own output, whether or not any other tool ran first. It also means the exported file is
something you can open and check — or edit — before feeding it onward; nothing happens behind
your back.

One convenience exists, and only inside TEST_LAB: if you ran ID Reconciliation earlier in the
same session, Data analysis recipe Scaffolding offers a checkbox to bake those reconciliation
steps straight into the generated data analysis recipe. You can still ignore it and choose your
own files — the checkbox is pure opt-in, and it never reaches across a user-space boundary.

## 5. Why most handoffs between spaces are a file, never a button

TEST_LAB, BLUEPRINT, and GALLERY are each turned on or off independently by their own feature
flag. A deployment can offer TEST_LAB without BLUEPRINT, or GALLERY without BLUEPRINT. An
in-app "Open in BLUEPRINT" button would break the moment BLUEPRINT is disabled for that
deployment — a file on disk works regardless of which spaces happen to be switched on. There
is no such button anywhere in the app.

| Handoff | How it works |
|---|---|
| TEST_LAB Scaffolding → BLUEPRINT | Export the boilerplate ZIP; open it in BLUEPRINT like any data analysis recipe, if BLUEPRINT is enabled. |
| BLUEPRINT → HOME | Save the data analysis recipe to disk; HOME's selector picks it up. |
| TEST_LAB Anonymiser → BLUEPRINT (de-anonymise later) | Join the anonymised data with the mapping TSV in BLUEPRINT, using the step printed in the Anonymiser's own output. |

Every row above reads the same way: export here, choose there. Nothing reaches across the
boundary on its own — except one case.

**The one real in-app handoff: GALLERY → HOME.** The "Clone to Sandbox" button in GALLERY sends
the example straight into HOME's "My view" (T3) sandbox as an audit node — no export, no file
to choose. It still respects the gating principle: it's only available when "My view" audit
capability is on (`t3_sandbox_enabled`) and the app features allows it, and the cloned node
starts with an empty, mandatory reason that blocks Apply until you fill it in — so nothing
reaches your results silently. There is no equivalent GALLERY → BLUEPRINT button; if you want
an example as a BLUEPRINT starting point, you copy its YAML text by hand, same as any file.
